title: Constrained mean-field control with singular control: Existence, stochastic maximum principle and constrained FBSDE
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a theoretical stochastic control problem rather than an educational intervention. Specifically, it studies constrained mean-field control (MFC) with singular control, where a social planner controls a McKean-Vlasov system subject to both dynamic state-control-law inequality constraints and a singular (bounded-variation) control component.

The authors first develop a relaxed control formulation to establish existence of optimal controls under these mixed constraints. They then derive a stochastic maximum principle (SMP) using a generalized Fritz-John/Lagrange multipliers approach and obtain an associated constrained backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE). Additional results establish uniqueness and stability for the resulting constrained forward-backward SDE system under stronger assumptions.

The work is entirely mathematical and does not involve human participants, schools, students, or any educational setting. Its main contribution is a set of existence, optimality, uniqueness, and stability results for constrained mean-field control with singular controls, expanding the theory beyond previously studied regular-control-only cases.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/mathematical control paper on constrained mean-field control and singular stochastic control, not an educational intervention study. It does not evaluate ChatGPT, LLM tutoring, or any K-12 learning technology, and provides no empirical design relevant to the retrieval topic.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational or student outcome, no intervention effect, and no evidence of impact on middle school mathematics or tutoring outcomes. The paper is irrelevant to the requested causal evidence question.
